Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-0-prompt-long-0121", "row_sha256": "889183f073039b889ee4050ae4ebaf52c3142d466d41296ae152a29846d21633", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "
could you turn these notes into a clear inventory handoff prompt for the receiving crew at Harbor Table Food Cooperative? the handoff is for Tuesday, 14 October 2025, and that crew arrives at 7:30 in the morning. The notes came from the closing count on Monday, 13 October, at 6:10 p.m. Jo and Mina did that count together. I need the prompt to ask for a handoff based on these notes, not to make the handoff itself here. There are several storage areas, so it would help if the listed products were grouped by where they are stored. You can sort the items by storage area, but do not modify records. Keep that restriction tied to the records; I mean the written inventory entries, not a ban on arranging the list for readability. Please make the request easy for someone on the receiving shift to follow, without turning the count into a claim that a delivery has arrived or that anything has been corrected.

For the dry store, the count says there are eight sealed bags of rolled oats, each marked 2 kg, plus one opened bag estimated at about 1.4 kg. The estimate is written as an estimate, not a weighed figure, and the note does not say how much was in that open bag before the count. There are eleven sealed 1 kg bags of brown lentils. One of the lentil bags is torn, and the note says its contents were transferred into a food-safe bin. It does not give the bin’s weight or say whether the torn bag is still included in the count of eleven, so don’t silently settle that point. The dry store shelf label reads “Grains and pulses,” although oats and lentils are listed in separate lines in Jo’s sheet. Keep those details clear if the prompt calls for them to be shown separately.

The back cooler notes list three crates of carrots, each carrying the lot tag C41, and each crate is marked 18 kg. The note records the three crates as present at closing; it does not give an individual net weight or say whether the crate weight is included. There are also two unopened cases of oat milk in the back cooler, with twelve cartons in each case. A third case is open and has seven cartons remaining. Mina said, “The second crate is still under the bench.” That is what she said during the count, and I want the quoted sentence retained as a note rather than treated as a separate verified count or a direction to move anything. The bench is in the back cooler area according to the sheet, but the sheet does not identify which product the second crate refers to, so leave that reference as it is.

There is a separate produce area near the market room entrance. It has two crates of pears. The handwritten card beside them says 24 kg, while the scale sheet for those same two crates totals 22.6 kg. The notes do not explain why those figures differ. Keep both figures and make clear that they come from different written sources; don’t choose one as correct or calculate a replacement. The scale sheet is dated Monday, 13 October, but there is no time written beside the pear figure. Jo’s closing count sheet has the 6:10 p.m. time at the top, not specifically beside every product. Please don’t imply that the scale reading was taken at exactly 6:10 if the notes do not say so.

The market room shelf also has six jars of tomato sauce, all labeled with the same batch code TS-08. The count says four jars are on the middle shelf and two are on the lower shelf. No jar is marked damaged, and there is no note about a use-by date. Do not add a date or a condition for them. The paper label on the middle shelf says “local preserves,” and the lower shelf label says “reserve stock.” Those labels describe the shelf locations as written; they do not identify a different sauce or a different batch. The point of mentioning both shelves is to make the placement easy to check on the receiving shift, not to suggest the jars should be moved.

One more note from the dry store says a delivery of sunflower seeds is expected later on Tuesday, but there is no delivery time and no quantity in the notes. It is an expectation recorded at closing, not confirmation that the delivery took place. There is no supplier name listed, and no one has written down a purchase order number. Mention the expected delivery as pending information if it belongs in the handoff, but don’t fill in a supplier, time, quantity, or arrival result. I also found a note saying the receiving crew should flag any count question to Jo; it does not say to hold all receiving work, contact a supplier, or change the closing count.

Please organize the request around the Tuesday receiving handoff and identify the closing count as the source for the listed stock. It should ask for the quantities, locations, labels, lot or batch codes, and unresolved differences to remain distinguishable. Keep the approximate oats amount approximate, keep the pear figures attributed to their respective records, and leave the question about the torn lentil bag and the reference to Mina’s second crate unresolved. The count and notes are the supplied information; don’t state that a later check has happened. Make room for the quote and the note to flag count questions to Jo, but don’t make either one sound like an instruction to move stock or stop work. I’m looking for one usable prompt in plain English, with sensible headings if helpful, not a completed inventory report or a recommendation about what the cooperative should do.", "output": "Draft a clear inventory handoff for the receiving crew at Harbor Table Food Cooperative, arriving Tuesday, 14 October 2025, at 7:30 a.m. Base it on the closing count recorded by Jo and Mina on Monday, 13 October, at 6:10 p.m. This is an inventory handoff based on the notes below; do not present any later check, delivery, correction, or other event as having happened.

You may group the listed items by storage area to make the handoff easier to use, but do not modify records. Keep the written inventory entries distinct from any organization of the list for readability. Use clear headings where helpful, and keep the quantities, locations, labels, lot or batch codes, and unresolved differences distinguishable.

Dry store
- Eight sealed bags of rolled oats, each marked 2 kg, and one opened bag estimated at about 1.4 kg. Keep the open-bag amount identified as an estimate. The notes do not say how much was in the bag before the count.
- Eleven sealed 1 kg bags of brown lentils. One bag is torn, and its contents were transferred into a food-safe bin. The notes do not give the bin’s weight or clarify whether the torn bag is included in the count of eleven; leave that point unresolved.
- The shelf label reads “Grains and pulses.” Jo’s sheet lists oats and lentils on separate lines.
- A delivery of sunflower seeds is expected later on Tuesday, according to a note made at closing. No time, quantity, supplier, or purchase order number is recorded. Present this as an expectation, not as confirmation that a delivery arrived, and do not fill in the missing details.

Back cooler
- Three crates of carrots, each carrying lot tag C41 and marked 18 kg. The notes record the crates as present at closing, but do not specify individual net weights or whether crate weight is included.
- Two unopened cases of oat milk, with twelve cartons in each case, and one open case with seven cartons remaining.
- Retain Mina’s note as a quote: “The second crate is still under the bench.” The sheet places the bench in the back cooler but does not identify which product the second crate refers to. Keep the reference unresolved; do not present it as a separately verified count or an instruction to move anything.

Produce area near the market room entrance
- Two crates of pears. The handwritten card says 24 kg, while the scale sheet for the same two crates totals 22.6 kg. Attribute the figures to their respective written sources, retain both, and do not choose between them or calculate a replacement. The scale sheet is dated Monday, 13 October, with no time beside the pear figure. Although Jo’s closing count sheet has 6:10 p.m. at the top, do not imply that the scale reading was taken at that exact time.

Market room shelf
- Six jars of tomato sauce, all labeled with batch code TS-08: four on the middle shelf and two on the lower shelf. The middle shelf label reads “local preserves,” and the lower shelf label reads “reserve stock.” Treat those as location labels, not as different sauces or batches. No jar is marked damaged, and the notes provide no use-by date; do not add a condition or date. Include the shelf locations to make the placement easy to check, not to suggest moving the jars.

Include the note that the receiving crew should flag any count question to Jo. Do not turn it into an instruction to stop receiving work, contact a supplier, or change the closing count. Keep the approximate oats quantity approximate, and leave both the torn-lentil-bag count question and Mina’s crate reference unresolved. Produce one usable prompt in plain English, not a completed inventory report or a recommendation about what the cooperative should do."}]
